title: Baked Mooncakes with Sweet Red Bean Paste
summary: Patterned golden mooncakes with a soft honey-enriched crust wrapped around a smooth sweet red bean filling.
equipment: baking tray lined with baking paper

ingredients.item: cake flour, plus more for dusting
fine sea salt or table salt
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Alkaline
steps.text: Boil 240 ml water with ½ tsp bicarbonate of soda, then simmer to reduce to about 2 tbsp over 7-8 min, cool and keep only ½ tsp.

steps.title: Dough
steps.text: Beat 147 g honey, the ½ tsp alkaline water, 66 g oil, 240 g cake flour and ½ tsp salt until smooth, then wrap and chill 30 min with the 340 g red bean paste in a covered bowl.

steps.title: Divide
steps.text: Divide the dough into 6 balls of 78-80 g and the bean paste into 6 balls of 56-60 g.

steps.title: Wrap
steps.text: On oiled cling film, roll each dough ball into a 6 mm disc, enclose a bean ball, seal, then roll round again.

steps.title: Press
steps.text: Press each ball into a floured mould onto a lined tray to imprint, re-flouring between cakes and spacing them 5 cm apart.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Freeze 5-10 min while the oven heats to 190 °C.

steps.title: Glaze
steps.text: Mix 1 egg, 1 egg yolk, 1½ tsp milk and ⅛ tsp salt and give each cake two thorough coats.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake 15-20 min until set and golden underneath, then cool fully on the tray before serving in wedges.

tips: Chill both the dough and the bean paste before shaping, as it makes wrapping the balls much easier.
Apply two full coats of egg wash for an even, glossy golden finish.
Re-flour the mould between each cake so the pattern releases cleanly every time.
safety: Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Store in an airtight container at room temperature for a few days, or chill or freeze for longer keeping, bringing back to room temperature before serving.
